We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some candidate building blocks from catalog searches:

- 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we have ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1 (chlorosulfonyl benzene) price $25.3 (25g). That's cheap.

- Aniline derivatives: Cc1ccc(N)cc1 (p-toluidine) price $28.6 for 1g.

- For the amide side chain: C=CC(=O)Nc1ccccc1N (trans-? Actually it's an anilide with terminal amine). We have NC1=CC=CC=C1NC(=O)C=C (same). Price $522 for 1g.

But our target has a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: tolyl sulfonamide attached to phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we can think retrosynthesis:

Step 1: Disconnection of sulfonamide bond: target -> sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph) + aniline (p-toluidine). Reaction: sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide.

Thus precursors: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl bearing the side chain (the other aromatic). The sulfonyl chloride is 4-(...?) Wait the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl that also has the side chain (aryl-sulfonyl). The sulfonyl chloride would be 4-(...?) Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to phenyl ring that also has the side chain (the aryl with the unsaturated amide). The sulfonyl chloride is 4-(...?) Let's examine target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So we have tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached via NH to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl (para-substituted) which has the side chain (C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). So the sulfonyl chloride needed is 4-(C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(styryl amide) benzenesulfonyl chloride). That may not be commercially available.

Alternative disconnection: break the C=C bond (Michael addition) to get aldehyde? Could do Wittig to install the double bond later.

Better: Use sulfonylation of aniline with sulfonyl chloride derived from the other aryl (with side chain). Could we instead form sulfonamide by reacting sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) with aniline (p-toluidine). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride: 4-(C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2) phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Might not be available.

Alternative: Use sulfonylation of aniline with sulfonyl chloride derived from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) and then later attach the other aryl via nucleophilic aromatic substitution? Not possible.

Maybe we can reverse: first form the amide side chain on aniline, then sulfonylate that aniline with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? But the sulfonamide attaches to the nitrogen of the aniline (the one bearing the side chain). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (p-toluidine) and the sulfonyl attached to the other phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is the aniline from tolyl. So we need to sulfonylate p-toluidine with aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl = phenyl with side chain). Could we generate that via chlorosulfonation of the phenyl with side chain? Starting from phenyl with side chain (the unsaturated amide). That phenyl is 4-(C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2) phenyl. Could we get that phenyl as a commercially available aryl? Probably not.

Alternative route: Use sulfonylation of the side-chain phenyl with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride, then later do a nucleophilic aromatic substitution? Not.

Maybe we can use a different disconnection: break the amide bond: target -> aniline (c3ccccc3N) + α,β-unsaturated acid (C=CC(=O)?) Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (aniline). So we can disconnect amide: get aniline (c3ccccc3N) and acid component: C=CC(=O) attached to phenyl sulfonyl aryl? Wait the amide carbonyl is attached to the side chain phenyl (the one bearing sulfonyl). The amide carbonyl is attached to the side chain phenyl via the carbonyl carbon, and the nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So the acid component is the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the phenyl sulfonyl aryl: /C=C/C(=O)- (attached to phenyl sulfonyl). So we could make that acid via oxidation of the corresponding aldehyde? Might be complex.

Given limited time, perhaps we can propose a 2-step route using commercially available building blocks:

Step 1: Perform a Suzuki coupling to attach the phenyl sulfonyl aryl to the tolyl sulfonamide? Not.

Maybe we can propose a convergent route: Start from p-toluidine (commercial) and 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-Br). Then sulfonylate to get p-tolyl sulfonamide with bromophenyl. Then do a Heck coupling to install the side chain (C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2) onto the bromophenyl. Then amide formation with aniline.

Thus steps:

1. Sulfonylation: p-toluidine + 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-Br) -> p-tolyl sulfonamide with bromophenyl (intermediate A). (ClSO2-Ph-Br is commercially available? We have ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1 (chlorobenzenesulfonyl chloride) but not brominated. Could we get 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Not in catalog yet. Could search.
